final_plan.guard_self_exemption:
Three mechanisms, none of them a list, all verified by running the scanner rather than reasoning about it.

1. PROSE IS NEVER SCANNED - file type, not exemption. _dev/primes/prime-shell-commands.md and skills/do-work/docs/prescribed-shell-primitives.md are .md; the walk is `git ls-files -- '*.sh'`. Markdown is outside the scope by construction; nothing has to know those files exist.

2. THE GUARD'S OWN FIXTURE IS NOT EXEMPTED - IT IS GENUINELY CLEAN. Both fixture heredocs interpolate the dangerous characters:

    local fixture_path="$1" pipe_character='|' hash_character='#'
    cat > "$fixture_path" <<FIXTURE
    tar tzf a.tgz $pipe_character grep --quiet marker
    $hash_character a comment between the pipe and the reader
    FIXTURE

so the audit file's own bytes never carry `| grep -q`. The offending shapes exist only in the temp file written at run time. VERIFIED: I built the complete audit file - doc comment block, both fixture writers, the named-shape table, a `grep -qx "$shape_line" <<<"$reported"` self-read, and the walk - and scanned it with the fixed scanner. Zero findings. It also passes `shellcheck --severity=warning`, the lane's exact invocation.

3. THE COMMENT RULE, AND THE PROOF IT CANNOT HIDE A RUNNING OFFENDER. A `#` suppresses exactly what bash suppresses:
  (a) `#` at the start of a logical line with no continuation pending - bash discards the line, nothing runs, the guard skips it. Moving a real offender there DELETES the check rather than hiding it; a vanished assertion is caught by the file's own behaviour, not the guard's job. There is no state where the offender is both hidden and live.
  (b) `#` reached while a continuation is pending - bash ends the COMMENT at the newline but the pipeline stays open and the next line is its right-hand side.

CASE (b) IS A REAL HOLE IN THE SHIPPED SCANNER. I confirmed it with bash, not by reading awk: `seq 1 5 |` / `# comment` / `grep -c .` prints 5, and the `| \` variant prints 5 too; `bash -n` accepts both. The shipped scanner MISSES both, because `joined_command == "" && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }` only skips a comment when nothing is pending - otherwise it concatenates the comment text and CLOSES the logical line there, building `tar tzf a.tgz |# an ordinary commentgrep -q marker`, where `commentgrep` no longer matches the grep token boundary.

THE FIX - two added awk lines inside the existing function, no new scanner:

    joined_command == "" && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
    {
      physical_line = $0
      if (joined_command != "") { sub(/#.*$/, "", physical_line) }   # NEW
      sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", physical_line)
      if (joined_command == "") { first_line_number = NR }
      if (joined_command != "" && physical_line == "") { next }      # NEW: stay pending
      ...

VERIFIED, ADDITIVE ONLY: catches both new comment shapes; still catches every other spelling; and BYTE-IDENTICAL output to the shipped scanner over all 93 tracked files (129 findings each, diff reports no difference). It reveals nothing new today, so it can safely land in the same commit as the move.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: stripping trailing `#` comments on non-continuation lines. It would kill a latent false-positive vector but introduce a false NEGATIVE one (`printf '#' | grep -q x` truncates to `printf '`) and would change today's behaviour. Fix only the hole that hides a running pipeline.

  A (23 lines)  `find ... -print -quit | grep -q .`  ->  `[ -n "$(find ... -print -quit)" ]`

                adds 2>/dev/null (target directory expected absent), and staged-skills:82 /
                install-suite:142 need find's status asserted (see the next field).

  B (100 lines) `printf '%s' "$v" | grep -q P`  ->  `grep -q P <<<"$v"`
                The producer is a builtin replaying an already-captured variable, so it carries no
                verdict; the real producer ran earlier inside $( ) and its status is asserted on the
                capture line in every case but two by design (qualify.sh:217 and :297, which measure
                warning text rather than exit code). Lossless. Preserve per site: $'...' ANSI-C
                patterns, BRE vs -E dialect, `--` end-of-options guards, and the two three-stage
                lines (audit-archive-timestamps.sh:170 and :195) which need an intermediate capture.

  C (6 lines)   Never a bare herestring - see sites_needing_an_explicit_status_assertion.

WHAT THIS SWEEP ACTUALLY FIXES, stated honestly: roughly 122 of the 128 _dev/tests sites are shape
conversions with no live defect. The defects are staged-skills-contract.sh:82 and install-suite-
behavior.sh:142 (already broken, reproduced with a stubbed find), and the 45 silent-pass-class sites
where a SIGPIPE death makes a real regression pass quietly - protected-inventory.sh:19, qualify.sh:183
and :368, staged-skills:60/269/308, and the refused-stamp checks in both timestamp files being the
ones guarding something worth guarding. Plan A said 28 of these; the measured number is 45.
sites_needing_an_explicit_status_asserti: _dev/tests/staged-skills-contract.sh:82-86 AND _dev/tests/install-suite-behavior.sh:142 - `find "$path" -type f ! -path ... -print -quit | grep -q .`. THE ONE ALREADY-BROKEN PAIR, and I reproduced it: a stubbed find that prints a leftover path and then exits 1 (the unreadable-subdirectory case) makes the pipeline nonzero under pipefail even though grep matched, so the guard stays SILENT and the suite reports the legacy runtime as retired while a file is sitting there. `grep -q . <<<"$(find ...)"` does NOT fix it - command substitution discards find's status too. The right conversion deletes the grep: `legacy_leftover_path="$(find ...)" || fail "could not scan $path"`, then `[ -n "$legacy_leftover_path" ]` in the compound condition. Naming the found path in the fail message is free.

_dev/tests/prescribed-shell-cases/qualify.sh:368 - producer is `git -C "$qualify_repo" diff --cached --name-only`, a NEGATIVE assertion that the fixture index stayed clean. A bare `grep -q 'cell_renderer' <<<"$(git ...)"` discards git's status, so a git failure becomes an unconditional pass on the check whose whole point is that the index is clean. Two steps: `qualify_staged_paths="$(git ...)" || fail_case 'could not read the fixture index'`, then herestring. Strictly better than today, which swallows the same failure via pipefail.

_dev/tests/staged-skills-contract.sh:60-61 - producer is `git check-attr export-ignore`. POSITIVE test for a FORBIDDEN state (it fails when the attribute IS set), so a dead producer yields no output, no match, and a SILENT PASS - the same class of narrowing REQ-593's review caught with the truncated tar. I measured the output at 36 bytes, so SIGPIPE is not the live risk; the dropped status is. Capture with `|| fail`, then herestring.
_dev/tests/install-suite-behavior.sh:135 - the identical `git check-attr export-ignore` shape and the identical silent-pass exposure. Same treatment.

_dev/tests/staged-skills-contract.sh:269-270 and :308-309 - producer is `sed -n '/^## Routing/,/^## Dispatch/p' skills/do-work/SKILL.md`, the IDENTICAL range extracted twice. Both are positive tests for a forbidden routing row. Capture once into $core_routing_section, guard `[ -n "$core_routing_section" ] || fail 'could not read the core Routing section'`, then two herestrings. The non-empty guard matters beyond the mechanical conversion: require_file at line 168 covers a missing file but not an unreadable one, and if either heading were renamed sed would print nothing, exit 0, and both contracts would pass vacuously. I measured the range at 1832 bytes. Converting both against one capture removes a duplicated producer as well as the pipeline.

_dev/tests/contracts/core-checks.sh:291-293 - producer is `git diff --cached --name-status --no-renames -- .env`. POSITIVE assertion, so a bare herestring still fails loud, but it reports 'wrong cached metadata' for what is really 'git broke'. Split the `git add -u`, the capture, and the text test into three separate elif legs. Note this same measurement is already read a third way at lines 100-107 (redirect to a file, IFS= read -r -d '') - three shapes for one question in one file.

_dev/tests/prescribed-shell-cases/audit-archive-timestamps.sh:170 and :195 - three-stage `printf | grep -E '(would repair|repaired) ' | grep -q REQ-nnn`. Converting only the first stage leaves `grep -E | grep -q`, where the middle grep is itself an early-leaving reader's writer, and the scanner still reports the line. Capture the filtered lines into a variable, then herestring the second grep. Do NOT collapse into one grep -qE 'A.*B' - that adds an ordering constraint the two-grep form does not have.

risks: R1 TWO THIRDS OF THE SWEEP IS HEAVY-ONLY. 90 of the 128 _dev/tests sites live in prescribed-shell-cases/, reached only via staged-skills-contract.sh:189, which probe-lanes.sh registers inside the heavy block; the harness exits 2 outside that tier. A sweep verified only in the fast tier leaves 90 conversions unproven. Mitigation: each case file runs standalone with DO_WORK_MAINTAINER_TIER=heavy bash <file> for per-step attribution, plus one full --heavy run before the guard lands.

R2 NEGATIVE ASSERTIONS ARE THE ONES THAT MATTER, AND THERE ARE MORE THAN PLAN A THOUGHT. Measured 45 silent-pass-class logical lines (35 with && fail, plus 10 in `if <matching grep>; then fail` form), not 28. Converting a positive site removes a spurious FAIL nobody misses; converting a negative site restores a check nobody knew was off. If the sweep is cut short, these go first: protected-inventory.sh:19, qualify.sh:183 and :368, staged-skills-contract.sh:60/82/269/308, install-suite-behavior.sh:135/142, and the refused-stamp checks in both timestamp files.

R3 THE SCANNER SPLITS ON A BARE PIPE. A `|` inside a quoted grep pattern creates a phantom stage. Measured: zero false positives across all 93 tracked files today. A future conversion written as `grep -qE 'a|grep -q b' <<<"$v"` would trip it. The failure is loud and attributable, not silent, and the existing BRE-alternation sites (repair-req-timestamps.sh:195, audit-archive-timestamps.sh:170) verified clean. Name the limitation in the guard's comment rather than adding a quote-aware lexer.

R4 THE READER SET IS grep/egrep/fgrep ONLY. rg -q, | head, sed -n '/x/{p;q;}', awk '/x/{exit}' and | read are the same condition with a different reader and are NOT covered. I swept the tree for all of them: the only genuine instance is install-suite-behavior.sh:410, verdict-inert. Adding them today buys one false positive and no true ones. Per prime-shell-commands.md the guard's comment states the CONDITION and marks the reader names illustrative, so the next person extends it when a real instance appears.

R5 HERESTRINGS APPEND A NEWLINE that printf '%s' did not. Behaviour-identical for grep -q / -qx / -qxF across every site here, and would not be for a byte-exact reader such as wc -c. The one line to re-read deliberately is select-simple-reqs-behavior.sh:401, grep -qx 'run_set: ' against an unterminated final line.

R6 NUL BYTES. Command substitution and herestrings both drop NULs. qualify.sh:418 asserts an untracked BINARY asset is NOT named; the captured variable holds qualify's report rather than the fixture's NULs, so it is safe, but re-run that specific case after converting.

R7 THE MOVE MUST NOT TAKE THE MATCHER SELF-CHECK WITH IT. verify_output_matchers_read_greps_verdict (update-script-behavior.sh:116-142) drives the two shipped matchers over a 256 KiB variable and is the only thing proving the mechanism on real data. It stays. Only the scanner, its two verify_ wrappers and its fixture move.

R8 THE GUARD MOVES FROM HEAVY TO FAST, so a violation now blocks every commit rather than only --heavy. Intended, and cheap (measured 0.24 s over 93 files against a 30 s per-file fast budget), but it changes when a violation is discovered and should be said out loud in the commit message.
R9 STEP ORDER IS LOad-BEARING. Step 13 (the shipped line + release) must land BEFORE step 14 (the repository-wide guard), or the gate is red between them.

R10 THE FIXTURE'S EXPECTED LINE NUMBERS ARE COUPLED TO THE FIXTURE HEREDOC. Adding a shape in the middle shifts every later number. Mitigation is already in the design: each number is paired with its shape name in one array next to the heredoc, so the edit is local and a mismatch names the shape rather than an arithmetic difference.
